items.title: Bulls return to Dalal Street; analysts see Nifty heading towards 23,800
items.description: Indian stock market is showing strong recovery, gaining for a second consecutive day. Investors are regaining confidence as crude oil prices cool and diplomatic talks are underway. Analysts predict the upward trend may continue, with potential for further gains in the coming days. Sectors like autos, metals, and BFSI are expected to lead this recovery.

items.title: UAE Central Bank clears Emirates NBD-RBL deal
items.description: The approval also covers the amalgamation of Emirates NBD's existing operations in India into RBL Bank, subject to the necessary regulatory clearances.

items.title: BlueStone rises 15% in a month as investors bet on scale-driven model amid improving store maturity
items.description: BlueStone Jewellery's shares have surged 15% in a month, outperforming the market. Analysts anticipate margin growth driven by operating leverage and store expansion, with over half of its 323 stores now achieving significant annual revenue. The company's revenue grew 34% year-on-year, while net losses narrowed considerably.

items.title: Vetting A/c to trace Rs 150 cr 'gone missing': Kotak Bank
items.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank is reconciling ₹150 crore in fixed deposits and accounts linked to the Municipal Corporation of Panchkula following allegations of missing funds. The bank has filed a police complaint and stated that all account processes and transactions were handled according to due process and banking norms.

items.title: Google to verify apps, help track finfluencers: Sebi
items.description: Sebi is collaborating with Google to combat financial influencers who break rules. Artificial intelligence will be used to identify and remove these individuals from online spaces. A verified badge is now available on Google Play for stock trading apps from registered entities. This initiative aims to protect retail investors from fraudulent apps and misleading content.

items.title: Framework to measure tech health of bourses on the cards
items.description: The market regulator has proposed an IT Resilience Index (ITRI) to assess the technology robustness of stock exchanges and other market infrastructure. This index will monitor the health of IT systems, with availability and security carrying the highest weightages. The framework aims to provide clearer insights into vulnerabilities and enable inter-institutional comparisons.

items.title: RBI may keep call rates and treps below the repo
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India aims to keep overnight borrowing costs below its main lending rate. This strategy supports economic growth despite rising imported inflation. Policymakers may overlook current high inflation figures. They are expected to maintain interest rates unchanged. This approach counters a slowdown and avoids hindering growth. Support from monetary and fiscal policies is expected to continue.

items.title: Nifty's rebound not enough to allay Dalal Street fears
items.description: Indian equities saw a relief rally with the Nifty climbing 3.5% in two sessions, fueled by optimism over de-escalation in West Asia and softening crude prices. However, the Volatility Index (VIX) only eased a modest 7%, indicating traders are maintaining hedges due to uncertainty about the sustainability of the current peace and the market's bottom.

items.title: UltraTech settles JAL dispute, agrees to redeem Rs 1k-cr shares
items.description: UltraTech Cement has finally settled a lengthy arbitration dispute with Jaiprakash Associates, paving the way for a fresh financial landscape. Under the newly minted agreement, ₹1,000 crore worth of preference shares tied to the Dalla Super cement project will be redeemed. This resolution is strategically aligned with the Adani Group’s recent acquisition, potentially easing their initial cash burden.

items.title: Prudential, HCL edge closer to health cover JV launch
items.description: Prudential Plc and HCL Group are close to launching their health insurance joint venture. Regulatory approvals are progressing well. Eased Press Note 3 rules are facilitating the deal. This partnership was delayed for over a year. The venture is structured as a 70:30 partnership. Relaxations in rules are expected to improve foreign investment.

items.title: Credit card spending moderates while banks keep adding users
items.description: February 2026 witnessed a subtle decline in credit card transactions compared to the previous month, January. Despite this, a year-on-year comparison reveals increased consumer spending. Banks are enthusiastically welcoming new credit card clientele, which hints at a thoughtful growth strategy. The sustained expansion is primarily fueled by advancements in digital services and e-commerce.

items.title: Real estate stocks tumble up to 32% in 2026: Time to buy ahead of RBI’s April MPC meeting?
items.description: Real estate stocks have seen significant declines, with the Nifty Realty index down 22% in 2026, due to concerns over IT layoffs and broader market weakness from the Iran-US war. Experts advise a selective approach, favoring quality large-cap players with balanced portfolios and potential growth in new geographies.

items.title: Fed chair nominee Warsh may need five years to really shrink the central bank’s balance sheet
items.description: Federal Reserve nominee Kevin Warsh aims to shrink the central bank's balance sheet, but a top economist suggests significant reforms are needed. Professor Darrell Duffie argues that overhauling bank liquidity rules and redesigning the payment system could take years, extending beyond Warsh's potential term.

items.title: Shri Ram Navami 2026: Are commodity markets MCX and NCDEX open today? Check 2026 holiday list
items.description: India's largest commodity exchange, MCX, will observe a partial trading holiday today for Shri Ram Navami, resuming in the evening. Equity markets NSE and BSE are fully closed. NCDEX will remain shut for the entire day. This follows a strong performance in Indian equity markets on Wednesday.

items.title: Stock Market Holiday: Are NSE, BSE open or closed today on 26 March for Ram Navami celebration? Check now
items.description: NSE Holidays 2026: Is there a stock market holiday today? ndian stock market exchanges NSE and BSE, will remain closed on Thursday on account of Shri Ram Navami

items.title: Gift Nifty slips over 100 pts on Iran-US uncertainty, rising oil prices. Will Sensex, Nifty snap 2-day rally on Friday?
items.description: Gift Nifty dropped over 100 points, indicating a weak start for Indian markets around 23,170. The fall comes as oil prices rebound amid uncertainty over Middle East tensions, with Iran still reviewing a US proposal to end the conflict.

items.title: Stock markets to remain shut on 3 days in 2 weeks; Nithin Kamath says best time to take a break after the mental toll
items.description: Indian stock markets will remain shut for three days over the next two weeks due to key holidays. Amid heightened global volatility, Zerodha CEO Nithin Kamath advised traders to prioritise capital preservation, reduce risk and take a break, highlighting the mental toll of trading in uncertain, headline-driven market conditions.

items.title: Brokerages initiate coverage on Fractal Analytics, Urban Company, Sagility, 8 other stocks with up to 40% upside. Do you own any?
items.description: A host of domestic and global brokerages have initiated coverage on select Indian stocks across sectors such as AI, defence, and home services. Analysts are bullish on major names such as Sagility and Solar Industries and forecast strong upside from current market levels. Here is a list of 11 stocks on which brokerages have initiated coverage.

items.title: Smallcap selloff! 10 stocks plunge up to nearly 70% in FY26. Do you own any?
items.description: Smallcap stocks have faced intense pressure in FY26, with sharp corrections driven by a mix of global and domestic factors. Rising U.S. tariff concerns, escalating geopolitical tensions, and higher crude oil prices have dented risk appetite, leading to heavy selling in the broader market. At the same time, elevated valuations in the smallcap space triggered profit booking, amplifying the downside. With volatility remaining high and investor confidence fragile, here are 10 stocks that saw massive selling.

items.title: Treason! Nobel laureate Paul Krugman claims people close to Trump behind $580-mn mystery bets before post on US-Iran talks
items.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has accused people close to former US President Donald Trump of insider trading, calling $580 million in pre-announcement oil and S&P futures bets “treason.” The trades were executed minutes before Trump’s post on US-Iran talks, triggering sharp market moves and raising serious national security concerns.

items.title: These 12 penny stocks rose up to 432% in FY26; 3 turned multibaggers.  Did you own any?
items.description: In the fiscal year 2026 (FY26), 12 penny stocks delivered impressive gains ranging from 25% to 432%, including three multibaggers. These outperformers were identified using specific filters: market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore, a share price under Rs 20, and a minimum trading volume of 5 lakh shares. This approach highlights low-priced, actively traded micro-cap stocks exhibiting strong upward momentum.Penny stocks continue to draw interest due to their low price points and high return potential. However, they come with substantial risk, marked by low liquidity, sharp volatility, and limited transparency. For investors, success in this space requires more than luck; it demands discipline, thorough research, and a firm grip on risk management. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: 2008-like crisis ahead? JPMorgan launches new way to bet against debt of Microsoft, Meta, Google; what this means
items.description: Investor anxiety is rising as oil prices surge amid the US-Iran conflict, while JPMorgan Chase has launched new credit default swaps allowing bets against the debt of major tech giants including Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle. The move echoes concerns of a 2008-style crisis as AI-driven borrowing accelerates.
